title: Obeticholic Acid
overview: On December 12, 2024, FDA issued a drug safety communication about cases of serious liver injury observed in patients without cirrhosis taking obeticholic acid to treat primary biliary cholangitis. Between May 2021 and September 2024, FDA identified 20 cases reporting one or more of the following events in patients treated with obeticholic acid: liver transplant, evaluation or listing for liver transplant, or liver-related death. Patients should talk to their doctor about risks versus benefits of taking obeticholic acid. Contact your doctor immediately is you notice any of the following: swollen belly; nausea, vomiting or diarrhea; yellowing of eyes or skin; bloody or black stools; coughing or vomiting up blood; loss of appetite or weight loss; new or worsening tiredness; weakness; fever or chills; lightheadedness; less frequent urination; mental status changes such as confusion, slurred speech, mood swings, personality changes, or increased sleepiness or difficulty waking up.

sections.Before taking obeticholic acid,: tell your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to obeticholic acid, any other medications, or any of the ingredients in obeticholic acid tablets. Ask your pharmacist for a list of the ingredients.tell your doctor and pharmacist what other prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take while taking obeticholic acid. Your doctor may need to change the doses of your medications or monitor you carefully for side effects. if you are taking cholestyramine (Prevalite®), colestipol (Colestid®), or colesevelam (Welchol®), take them at least 4 hours before or 4 hours after obeticholic acid.the following nonprescription product may interact with obeticholic acid: caffeine supplements. Be sure to let your doctor and pharmacist know that you are taking this medication before you start taking obeticholic acid. Do not start this medication while taking obeticholic acid without discussing with your healthcare provider.tell your doctor if you have bile duct obstruction (blockage in the tubes that carry bile from the liver to the gallbladder and small intestine). Your doctor may tell you not to take obeticholic acid.tell your doctor if you have ever drunk large amounts of alcohol, or if you have or have ever had high cholesterol or thyroid disease.tell your doctor if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking obeticholic acid, call your doctor.
